rows.what the ink shows: The overwritten first capital retains an upper upright with a long top arm and a shorter middle arm; the added lower foot belongs to the overlapping correction E. The deleted F is distinguishable, though the middle is dense.
A separate left upright extends below the two arms of the corrected F and turns into a lower rightward foot/loop. This lower arm supports the deleted E despite the heavy overlap.

After a clear 2, the last digit has a strong upper slant, middle bar and right downstroke, with a second inner lower hook. These overlapping strokes do not securely distinguish 5 from 4; the clean same-page 5 forms have a clearer bottom bowl.

rows.reading: \unsure{pour raison de continuité|par raison de continuité}
rows.what the ink shows: The opening p descender survives, but its following letters merge with the long cancellation. Upper letter fragments and the tall t near the right margin remain visible; they do not establish the whole cancelled phrase or distinguish pour from par.
The cancelled short word retains the hooked upper portion of s and a separate i dot to its right. The strike covers the lower bodies but the two-letter arrangement remains visible.

The superscript is a curved cap with a short descending right end, matching the compact 2 powers on the neighboring L terms, rather than a single upright 1. The baseline contains L followed by the parenthesized E, comma and G.
A tall p stem returns through a low loop into a nearly level rightward tail. The tail does not separate a terminal r from an s or establish the rest of the word securely.

The deletion leaves a looped initial with an ascending stroke and a low final upturn, but two heavy crossing lines cover the intervening letter bodies. The proposed donc cannot be recovered letter by letter.
Beneath the cancellation, a small rounded first bowl is followed by a deeper open-bottom trough rising at the right; the second letter has the cup of u rather than a visible n arch.
A short heavy horizontal stroke meets a thick descending curve with a rightward foot. Overwriting prevents separating a first a and a following l with confidence.

The small independent stroke before A descends and curves right at its foot, forming an opening parenthesis. Its hooked outline matches the opening parenthesis before G on the same line; there is no second quantifier arm or internal crossbar.
The space after prop. and before the closing parenthesis is crossed by a heavy continuous deletion line. No independent numeral stem survives clearly enough to settle 1.

On the canceled baseline a small v is followed by the descending stem of p and then a second v with a separate multi-ray superscript star. The long strike covers most strokes of remplacer and par; the star belonging to the inserted w=v* above is a separate layer.

Inside the canceled parenthetical, the horizontal strike leaves only a short upright remnant near the middle and overlapping lower loops near the right edge. These remnants do not identify the enclosed token.

The opening parenthesis, small bowl of v, membership-shaped stroke and final upright F with two rightward arms remain visible. Dense crossed loops obscure the middle E/bar/tensor region, so those components are not secured.
The canceled word starts with a tall stem and small closed upper loop forming P, unlike a rounded O. A short hooked final stroke survives at the right of the cancellation.
Below the first barred a, a hooked diagonal and thick zigzag cancellation cover the subscript. No independent slender numeral 1 can be separated from those strokes.
The subscript beside b is a compact dark knot with a descending hook; the overlapping cancellation hides the original numeral outline.
The second b has a separate short upright prime and a conspicuous horizontal overbar spanning the b and prime; the bar is not merely a prime stroke.

One u and one v followed by a raised star precede the equals sign; the parenthesis pair has its prime after the second a, followed by a visibly barred b. Crossing strokes and the final round knot do not separate a prime, tensor sign and terminal b; all candidate terminal material remains uncertain, and no terminal b is asserted.
The crossed prefix retains the long curved top and descending stem of T, followed by the short shoulder and trailing curve of r.

The two baseline a bowls, comma, and separate upright prime after the second a are visible. A short right arm and downward stem project above the first a, but their upper-left junction merges with diagonal cancellation, leaving a damaged star and a deletion spur indistinguishable.

An initial loop and upright resembling P survive, as does a sloping accent above the right-hand portion. The long heavy cancellation merges the intervening letter bodies, preventing a secure reading of both words.
